narration: S01.1 Tessa's mortgage fallback costs $120 a month.
S01.2 She's borrowing $320,000, and in her city that payment is her biggest bill.
N1-s01-stack.muted_read: A faceless figure by her house; a thin stack of bills appears beside the house and grows by one bundle on each beat, with a monthly price over it.

narration: S06.1 At 7.4 percent, finishing that loan in 15 years takes $2,948 a month.
S06.2 That's $120 a month more than the 15-year loan, for the same house and the same 15 years.
S06.3 Over those 15 years, the extra adds up to $21,622.
N1-s06-stack.muted_read: The 30-year bar is raised to finish in 15 years and ends just above the 15-year bar; the sliver above becomes bills that drop onto the stack, month after month, until it stands at its full height.

narration: S21.1 Back to Tessa's own loan, and a shortcut many people reach for: pay the 30-year exactly what the 15-year would cost, and assume it ends on the same day.
S21.2 At the October eighth rates, it doesn't: it ends about 15 months late.
S21.3 To finish in 15 years, she'd add $733 a month on top of the required payment.
N1-s21-track.muted_read: A month track runs from Tessa's house: 180 tiles, then 15 more tiles light in warn past the 15-year mark. Then a thin extra slab on top of the required payment makes the track end exactly at 180.

narration: S23.1 Tessa has another practical question: could she send the extra once a year instead of every month?
S23.2 That's one payment a year, the same total as the monthly extra.
S23.3 Paid that way, the loan ends four months later.
N1-s23-track.muted_read: On the month track, extra principal arrives as one big block every 12th tile instead of thin slabs; the track ends 4 tiles later.

narration: S25.1 Every extra dollar of principal stops interest from being charged on that dollar, at the loan's own rate.
S25.2 On Tessa's 30-year, that's 7.4 percent a year, before taxes.
S25.3 It isn't an investment return; it's interest she no longer pays.
S25.4 That rate is the bar any other use of that dollar gets measured against, before taxes.
S25.5 Whether any investment clears it, once risk and taxes count, isn't tested here.
N1-s25-bar.muted_read: A horizontal beam rises beside the house to the height of the loan rate; a single extra dollar sits on top of it; a second dollar, labelled "any other use", is held up against the beam.
